content:
- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after recent spikes.
- Forecast tends to peak too early and then sharply decline, missing the true mean-reversion path.
- Model underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the 30-day window, particularly when true values are rising.
- Overshoots occur after sharp upward moves in history; model reacts too aggressively, peaking too high.
- Model exhibits persistent downward bias in the middle of the forecast horizon, especially when true values are stabilizing.
- Model fails to capture mean reversion in the final 5–10 days, often underestimating the return to prior levels.
- Forecast lags behind true values by 2–5 days in the middle of the horizon, especially after volatility spikes.
- Model overreacts to recent low values, leading to premature correction and underestimation of subsequent recovery.
